findings.summary: 16 tracks with almost identical fees and no recommendation, so the reader couldn't choose without a familiar name. This blocks the decision. It is not the alphabetical-sort problem or the filter-chip problem.
Most rows in the returns column show 'less than 3 years' instead of a return, so a main figure can't be compared.
Fees are shown only as percentages, with no amount in shekels. This is a wish for more information, not a blocker.
There's no link or button to open an account or contact Harel. This is a missing extra; the comparison itself still works.
A table row is cut off between screens, so one track's name and numbers never appear together. It affects one row only, and the cause is the screen split.
Jargon in the exposure column headers (exposure to stocks and foreign currency) and unexplained ring charts leave the reader unable to understand a main column.
A long list of folded document sections whose titles don't say why to open them. This is a minor annoyance in secondary content.
